recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future defects in detailed cross-version package behavior should be fixed in the relevant xver package or targeted issue rather than duplicating package-guide prose back into core.
issue_request: FHIR-44614 asked to replace the older statement that implementations should use the correct element when present with SHALL-level guidance to use the equivalent element and to reserve cross-version extensions for missing elements, missing types, or max-cardinality changes from 1 to *.
initial_application: No commit explicitly names FHIR-44614, but commit 643dba42aa5d9eb8324e1390b7b194f737913bc5 changed source/versions.html the day after the FHIR-I vote from the old should/correct-element sentence to the requested SHALL/equivalent-element and allowed-cases wording.
additional_context: The Jira comment links HL7/fhir#3967. That PR merged f45505e5b3aa0d87effb991938750e627b782d2d, which intentionally pulled detailed cross-version content from the core versions page and pointed to individual cross-version definition packages. The current combined branch includes related FHIR-44615 and FHIR-42924 audit/fix commits and retains the concise rule that extensions are only defined when target-version data representation is unavailable.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the current build-scope source/versions.html no longer contains the obsolete sentence and already names the same missing-element, missing-type, and max-cardinality cases requested by the issue.
